_anchors.canvas.w: 64, the cruise's cell. Every clip of one subject shares one cell or the layers disagree about the origin.
_anchors.canvas.h: 48, the cruise's cell — sized by the ROLL clip's quarter-turn sweep, which is the worst pose of the subject, not of this clip.
_anchors.frames.walk: 9, and it is the inclusive count for eight intervals: a once-played clip's frame times are k/(n-1), so five phases at the quarters need (n-1) divisible by four. The contract lock refused 8 on the skate's ollie for exactly this.
_anchors.light.x: -0.5, the subject's lamp — all three clips share it or the plane changes colour mid-trick.
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.14 turn: the climb's largest hull key is 0.32, which is 16° of pitch — a zoom climb's real attitude, and about what the ollie spent on the deck. DERIVED for this action, not carried from the cruise's 0.05: run 7 lost a limb to exactly that carry.
_anchors.gait.lift: 2.4 px. The runtime displaces the whole sprite through the arc; the clip itself barely moves the hull.
_anchors.gait.roll: 0, AND THIS ZERO IS THE CONTROL: the climb is authored entirely on Bone.angle, the channel proven since run 5. If this clip reads worse than the shelf's other screen-plane jumps, the roll work damaged the old path — a rollback, not a tune. The skate's ollie ran the same duty.
_anchors.body.scale: 1, the subject's scale — a clip's tunables do not get to own how big the body is.
_anchors.fill.x: 0.45, opposite the key, as the cruise.
_anchors.fill.z: -0.3, matching the key, as the cruise.
_anchors.fill.weight: 0.1, the street's value, as the cruise.
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 75: nine frames make a 600 ms clip, sized to the first impulse's hang — 2·150/430 = 0.70 s — so the plane is level again just before it lands back on its line. Played once; holds the last frame.
